subject: Boundary Agent Key Broker: credential proxying and tenant egress playbook

Subject: Tenant isolation + BYOK proxying questions for private deployment

Hi Stephanie / Priyom,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As we scope the on-prem deployment for Citrine, a few follow-ups from infra: we need a concise design that explains how Redwood would: 1) allow our tenant to bring keys (BYOK) while preventing cross-tenant key access on the same host; 2) proxy key material or wrapping operations (we don't want raw key material exported from our HSM); and 3) provide telemetry logs that demonstrate key-use events for compliance teams (who will expect evidence for every unseal/sign operation).

Our constraints: we are air-gapped inside a healthcare VPC, egress is only allowed to a handful of outbound IPs (for patching and CRLs), and any secret-handling agents must run under our operator accounts.

Can you provide a short architecture sketch (diagram + dataflow notes) and a recommended rotation/custody policy we can put into our compliance pack? Also attaching our initial requirements sheet.

Attachments: Citrine-KMS-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Best,
Daniel

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@citrinehealth.com>; stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant isolation + BYOK proxying questions for private deployment

Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Putting some initial notes below; will turn this into a 1-tab diagram and an ops checklist by Tuesday.

Summary of the proposed approach (Boundary Agent Key Broker - BAKB):
- Local key custody: customer HSM remains the single source of truth; Redwood runs a thin Boundary Agent inside the tenant VPC that never stores unwrapped key material.
- Ephemeral wrapping tokens: Redwood issues short-lived wrap tokens (signed assertions) from the private control plane which the Boundary Agent redeems locally to perform KMS operations. Tokens are single-use for a session (TTL: 60s) and scoped to specific cryptographic operations (encrypt/decrypt/sign).
- Proxying pattern: all high-sensitivity calls (raw unseal, private key extraction) are executed by the Boundary Agent via direct HSM APIs under customer-managed operator credentials; Redwood only receives signed attestations that an operation completed (statement + HSM attestation blob). No raw key material crosses tenant boundary.
- Network egress: Boundary Agent will only reach Redwood control plane endpoints over TLS mutual-auth; we will support IP whitelisting and mTLS with client certs generated in your KMS during provisioning. If your policy forbids any outbound, we can switch to a pull-poll model via an on-prem control queue (signed messages).
- Rotation & custody cadence: recommend customer-controlled rotation every 90 days for KEKs (wrapping keys). For HSM master keys follow vendor best-practice (typically annual ceremony). Token keypairs used for mTLS are rotated at 30 days with automated re-provisioning hooks.

Compliance telemetry (what we can provide):
- Per-operation audit envelope: timestamp, operation type, caller identity (tenant operator id), HSM attestation hash, operation result.
- Signed chain-of-custody logs: boundary agent signs local events and streams them to an internal audit collector in the VPC; Redwood accepts only the signed envelopes (we do not store plaintext secrets).
- Proof artifacts: we can include HSM attestation blobs (vendor-specific), and a redacted evidence bundle suitable for SOC2 reports.

Open questions for Citrine: 1) Do you require HSM vendor-attestation verification in our control plane or will local verification by your team suffice? 2) Which outbound IP restrictions (if any) are absolutely non-negotiable?

I'll produce a one-page diagram and a short CAN (control/agent/network) checklist by Tue 05/12. If helpful, let's do a 30m follow-up on Mon.

— Priyom
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Daniel — thanks for the packet and the constraints. Priyom and Marcus have the right plan outlines. Next steps and owner assignments below so your team has clear artifacts for compliance: 

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Priyom: one-page architecture diagram (dataflow + network rules), and a CAN checklist (Control endpoints, Agent config, Network ACLs) — due 2026-05-13 EOD.
- Priyom: sample audit envelope JSON schema and a redacted evidence bundle template for SOC2 — due 2026-05-14.
- Marcus: draft MOU with two options (1) whitelist egress + mTLS client certs; (2) fully offline pull-proxy engagement estimate — due 2026-05-15.
- Citrine (Daniel): confirm absolute outbound IP restrictions and whether your security team requires vendor-side verification of HSM attestation blobs.

Notes on recommended config that should go into the ops checklist:
- Agent runs under customer operator identity; no long-term credentials are embedded.
- Wrap token issuance is authenticated by customer-supplied cert during provisioning; tokens are single-use and limited to a single HSM operation type.
- All audit envelopes are written to local immutable storage (WORM) for 90 days and streamed to your SIEM; Redwood only retains the signed envelopes (no plaintext keys).
- Key rotation policy: KEK rotate 90 days; mTLS certs rotate 30 days; HSM master follows vendor timeframe. Include a backup-unseal playbook for emergency operatorless recovery (documented but gated).

I'll attach the diagram and the checklist as soon as Priyom posts them to the runbook folder. For visibility I've shared the Drive folder link below — will add Citrine with view-only access once we get your OK on the egress rules.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_example_runbook
